items.title: Shane Wright Gets Much Needed Fresh Start With Kraken Trade To Predators
items.desc: During his time with the Seattle Kraken, Shane Wright never lived up to the expectations that come with being the fourth-overall pick. Now with a trade to the Nashville Predators, the 22-year-old has the opportunity to capitalize on a fresh start and redefine…

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Seattle has traded Shane Wright to Nashville for Matthew Wood, and Daily Faceoff describes it as a swap of former first-round picks that gives Wright a change of scenery. Wright went fourth overall in 2022, and Wood went 15th in 2023.

The numbers say this is a swap of two similar, slumping players. So far this season, Wright has 3 goals in 14 games against 3.74 expected goals (the number of goals a player's shot quality would typically produce), a shortfall of 0.74. Wood has 1 goal against 3.12 expected, a gap of 2.12. In that sense Wood has been the unluckier finisher, and his scoring should drift up if his chances keep coming. Both sit below even at five-on-five, with Wright at 47 percent of expected goals and Wood at 47 percent, and both play about 14 minutes a night. Seattle is 8-5-1 despite a 44.9 percent expected goal share, helped by 10.7 more goals than expected. We'd read that as a team outperforming its chances, so the Kraken's record is sturdier than their process. Nashville is 5-4-5 with a 48.9 share, a bit better than its results. Neither player moves the needle much on his own, but Wright gets a new look in Nashville.

stories.take:
Per ESPN, a Long Island cancer center unveiled a room dedicated to the late mother of Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer on Monday. It's a human story first, and it lands on a player already carrying a lot for his team.

Schaefer, the No. 1 pick in 2025, has 14 points in 14 games so far this season and plays 26.8 minutes a night. His goals (4) sit almost exactly where his chances say they should be, so this isn't a hot streak waiting to cool. The NYI also take a bigger share of the quality chances at 5-on-5 with him on the ice: 54 percent, and the team's share of that is about six percentage points better with him out there. That matters because the NYI as a whole sit at 46.5 percent of expected goals (the quality of chances) in all situations. Their 7-5-2 record owes a lot to goaltending, which has saved 10 goals more than expected so far this season. Schaefer is one of the few things driving play the right way.

items.title: Hockey Canada hires Dustin Schwartz as head of goaltending
items.desc: Schwartz formerly served as the goaltending coach of the Edmonton Oilers.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Hockey Canada has hired Dustin Schwartz as its head of goaltending. Schwartz was most recently the goaltending coach of the Edmonton Oilers, per the outlet's summary.

The move matters for Edmonton because the Oilers have been winning, but not mostly because of their goaltending. EDM is 11-2-2 and has controlled 53% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality, not just shot volume) so far this season. Yet the team's goalies have saved 2.6 fewer goals than expected given the shots they faced, so the results have come from elsewhere. EDM has scored 17 more goals than its chances would predict, which suggests finishing is carrying the record. At five-on-five the Oilers hold only 49% of the expected goals, so the edge comes from the power play (0.91 expected goals per game), not even-strength play. It's a small sample, but if the goaltending doesn't improve, the cushion may be thinner than 24 points in 15 games suggests.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Nikita Kucherov has requested a trade from the Lightning, and Daily Faceoff says he addressed it publicly for the first time on Monday, calling it a result of "poor communication and respect." The Athletic also quotes him saying Tampa Bay "made it clear that I'm free to walk on July 1," and cites one NHL GM estimating "31 teams" would pursue him if he's available.

Whatever the dispute, the on-ice case for him holds up. So far this season he has 4 goals and 14 assists in 13 games, and his own expected goals (a measure of the quality of his chances) come to 4.18 against 4 actual goals, so he's scoring about what his shots warrant. TBL controls 59% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice, and the team's share is about six points better with him out there than without him. Tampa Bay sits 8-3-2, and its expected-goals share of 56% says the record is earned. The weak spot is goaltending, where the team is 4 goals saved below expected, so Kucherov is driving a good team, not propping up a poor one.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Maple Leafs have placed forward Bo Groulx on waivers, noting he has played sparingly for Toronto this season and has yet to register a point. Groulx, drafted 54th overall by the Ducks in 2018 out of Halifax, has played 7 games so far this season.

The numbers back up the quiet stretch. Groulx has averaged 8.04 minutes a game and has no goals or assists. His own expected goals, a measure of the quality of the chances he has taken part in, sit at 0.07, so he has not been robbed of much offense. At 5-on-5, TOR has had 37.93% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share has been 8.65 points better when he is off it. That is a small sample, but it points to a depth forward who has not moved the play in the right direction. For fantasy purposes, he holds no value as a 0-point player in limited minutes. For the Leafs, the larger issue is a team at 47.7% of expected goals overall, and a roster spot like this one hardly decides that.

Daily Faceoff reports that Sabres forward Konsta Helenius is out week-to-week with an upper-body injury, and that Zach Benson also missed Monday's practice, with the team hoping it was only a maintenance day. Heather Engel of NHL.com posted that coach Lindy Ruff called Benson day to day.

Helenius is the smaller loss. He has 3 points in 11 games so far this season, and his own expected goals (the quality of his chances) are 1.15 against 1 goal scored. Benson is the one to watch. His 2 goals trail his expected total of 5.96 by almost 4, so his 13 points mostly come from setting up others. BUF controls 62 percent of the expected goals when he's on the ice at 5-on-5, and his team's share is about 17 points better with him out there. BUF sits at 50 percent overall, so he matters.

In the 2 games without Helenius, Jason Zucker has taken his spot beside Norris, Peyton Krebs is up to 15:48 a night from 11:59 and Sam Carrick is up to 8:11 from 5:46. If Benson sits, going by how the coach has used his players, Ryan McLeod is next in line for his minutes and Jiri Kulich is the likeliest to move into his power-play role.

His absence costs depth more than scoring, and it comes while PIT (5-7-2) sits near even at 49 percent of expected goals. Going by games already played without him, Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Dewar and Lizotte, Malkin is up to 17:08 a night from 14:56, and Tommy Novak is up to 17:31 from 15:25. items.desc: Journeyman goalie Matt Tomkins stopped 27 of the 28 shots he faced to help the Oilers beat the Rangers in just his seventh NHL start.

stories.take:
ESPN reports that journeyman goalie Matt Tomkins, from Sherwood Park, stopped 27 of 28 shots to lead the Oilers past the Rangers in his seventh NHL start.

Our numbers back up a strong night, with a caveat. Tomkins's .964 save percentage this season comes from one game in our data. Goals saved above expected, which measures how many more goals a goalie stopped than an average goalie would have against the same shots, was +1.44 for him, so he was well ahead of what those chances should have produced. That matters for EDM, whose team goaltending sits at -2.6 by the same measure so far this season. The Oilers are 11-2-2, with 17 more goals than expected, and their 49 percent share of expected goals at five-on-five (the quality of chances they create against what they allow) is below even. They have been winning on finishing, so a goalie who bails them out helps. One start won't settle it, but if Tomkins keeps stopping more than he should, that gap closes.

Our numbers show why this is a small loss on the ice. In four games so far this season, McIlrath averaged 6.58 minutes with no points. The team's share of expected goals (a measure of chance quality) was 51.45 percent at five-on-five while he played, but Washington's overall share of chances ran 1.46 points better with him off the ice. The sample is tiny, so we wouldn't read much into it, but nothing suggests the Capitals lose something real. They are 8-5-0 with a 53 percent five-on-five expected goal share, and their goaltending has saved 2.9 goals more than expected, which is propping up the record more than the scoring has. Losing a depth defenseman who barely played shouldn't change that picture.

stories.take:
The Hockey News reports that Lightning GM Julien BriseBois is drawing another hard line in contract talks, this time with Nikita Kucherov, after Tampa Bay moved on from Steven Stamkos. As Daily Faceoff's Leafs coverage posted, Elliotte Friedman reports Toronto is among the teams Kucherov would consider being traded to.

On the ice, Kucherov looks every bit the player worth the fight. He has 18 points in 13 games so far this season, and his goals (4) sit almost exactly on his expected goals (4.18), which measures the quality of his chances. So the production is real, not a hot streak. When he plays at 5-on-5, TBL controls about 59% of the expected goals, and the team's share is about six points better with him out there. That matters because TBL's goaltending has been a problem: the team is 4 goals saved above expected in the red. The skaters are carrying it, and Kucherov leads them.

Stamkos is a useful contrast. His 8 goals beat his expected 5.53 by nearly two and a half, and NSH's 5-on-5 share is lower with him on the ice. We'd call his start more fortunate than dominant.

Larkin's results undersell his play so far this season. He has 2 goals in 10 games, but his own expected goals (a measure of the quality of his chances) come to 3.03, so he is about one goal short of what those chances should have produced. Detroit controls 56.3% of the expected goals at 5-on-5 when he plays, and the team's share improves by 1.53 percentage points with him on the ice. Last season he scored 34 goals and 67 points in 74 games. For a buyer, that points to a player whose scoring should recover, though ten games is a small sample. As for Detroit, its 53.3% share of expected goals is solid, but it sits 7.2 goals below expected, which is part of why the record is a modest 6-5-3. Moving Larkin would remove a top-line forward who is still driving play.

The Hockey News adds that he is the reigning Hart winner, and Daily Faceoff posted that Kucherov called the request a result of "poor communication and respect."

Nothing in our numbers suggests a player on the decline. Through 13 games so far this season, Kucherov has 4 goals and 14 assists for 18 points, and he's scoring about exactly as often as his chances say he should (4 goals against 4.18 expected goals, which measures the quality of his shots). At five-on-five, TBL generates 58.83% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share is 6.17 percentage points better with him out there than without him. That is the profile of a driver, not a passenger.

It matters because TBL is 8-3-2 with a 55.6% expected goal share, yet has saved 4 fewer goals than expected in net, so the skaters are carrying the team. Losing his 20.98 minutes a night would hit a team already leaning on its offense.

The bigger question for Toronto is what the team around him looks like. TOR sits at 7-6-2 with 16 points through 15 games, but our numbers see a team playing worse than that record. Its share of expected goals, which measures the quality of chances for and against, is 47%, and it drops to 45% at five-on-five, so the Leafs are being outchanced in most of their even-strength minutes. They have scored 9.8 more goals than their chances would predict, and goalies have stopped 2.2 more than expected, so finishing and goaltending are both helping. Special teams are fine: the power play generates 0.71 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allows 0.75. The record is outrunning the underlying play so far this season, and a new forward alone won't close that gap.

items.title: Senators' Hayden Hodgson suspended 2 games for hit on Kings' Brandt Clarke

stories.take:
ESPN reports that Ottawa forward Hayden Hodgson was suspended two games by the NHL's Department of Player Safety for charging and boarding Los Angeles defenseman Brandt Clarke. The Athletic notes he drew a five-minute major and a game misconduct on the play, and Daily Faceoff adds he has no suspension history but was fined for boarding in the 2025 preseason.

For Ottawa, the loss is small. Hodgson, who was never drafted and came up as a free agent via the ECHL, has played about 5.1 minutes a game and has no points in five games so far this season. His 5-on-5 expected goal share (the share of scoring chances, weighted by quality, that his team gets while he's on the ice) is 41 percent, and the Senators' share improves by 9.2 points when he sits. The Senators (8-5-1) sit at 50 percent at 5-on-5, so this barely dents them. It matters more for Los Angeles. Clarke has been a real driver so far this season: a 56 percent share at 5-on-5, a 15-point team swing when he plays, and nine points in 12 games for a 4-6-2 club that needs him in the lineup.

items.desc: In this edition of The Hockey News Morning Skate, Eric Cruikshank and Michael Traikos break down Devin Cooley's injury in the Edmonton Oilers' win over the Calgary Flames, Sergei Bobrovsky's struggles against the Seattle Kraken, and more.

stories.take:
The Hockey News' Morning Skate reports that Calgary goalie Devin Cooley was injured in the Oilers' win over the Flames, and that Sergei Bobrovsky struggled against Seattle. The write-up doesn't say how serious Cooley's injury is.

If he's out, it hurts. Cooley has been a bright spot in a rough start for CGY. His goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops compared with an average goalie facing the same shots) is +2.19 in seven games so far this season, on top of a .912 save percentage. Last year he was +17.23 over 31 games. As a team, Calgary sits at -5.5 in that measure and is 5-7-0, so the goaltending has not been the problem when he plays. Without him, that picture could change quickly.

Bobrovsky's .885 save percentage looks ugly, but his goals saved above expected is +0.92 in 10 games, so he has been a bit better than the shots he's faced. That's a far cry from last season's -13.5 over 52 games. We'd call this a slow start with some luck-adjusted support, not proof the decline is over.
